scan.target_cidr.label: Target Subnet CIDR / Host IP
scan.target_cidr.meaning: Specifies the IPv4 network boundary or single machine address to probe for agentless WinRM endpoints, bounded by SSRF filters that block AWS/Azure/GCP cloud metadata addresses (169.254.169.254).
scan.target_cidr.format: CIDR notation (e.g. 10.20.30.0/24) or single host IP (e.g. 10.20.30.15)

scan.protocol.label: Agentless Protocol
scan.protocol.meaning: Determines the transport mechanism for remote CIM introspection: choose WinRM HTTPS (port 5986) for modern firewalled Windows 10/11 and Server 2016+ environments with TLS 1.3 encryption, or select WMI/DCOM (port 135 + dynamic high RPC ports) only for legacy Windows Server 2008/2012 systems lacking PowerShell Remoting.
scan.protocol.example: winrm_https (Port 5986 - Recommended for single-port firewall traversal)

scan.profile.label: Scan Profile
scan.profile.meaning: Controls the depth of WMI/CIM classes queried during the run, balancing execution duration against compliance depth.
scan.profile.example: full_hardware_os (Full Hardware, OS, BitLocker, Defender, & CIS Audit)

scan.vault_secret_ref.label: Credential Vault Reference
scan.vault_secret_ref.meaning: An opaque reference pointer to encrypted Active Directory Domain Admin or local administrator credentials stored in the AES-256-GCM Vault Manager, ensuring passwords never travel across the network in plaintext.

scan.gateway_id.label: Collector Gateway
scan.gateway_id.meaning: The local subnet worker daemon that receives encrypted job tasks via mTLS and executes local WinRM HTTPS requests inside the target network segment.

audit.bitlocker.label: BitLocker Volume Encryption Audit
audit.bitlocker.meaning: Queries Win32_EncryptableVolume to verify volume encryption method, protection status (XTS-AES 128/256), and key protector presence for all fixed NTFS/ReFS drives.

audit.software.label: Installed Software & Hotfixes Audit
audit.software.meaning: Enumerates 32-bit/64-bit Uninstall registry hives and Win32_QuickFixEngineering to index application packages, build versions, and security hotfix KB numbers.

audit.services.label: Windows Services & Startup Audit
audit.services.meaning: Scans Win32_Service for service display names, startup types (Automatic/Manual/Disabled), binary paths, and running account security contexts.

audit.tpm_bios.label: BIOS & TPM 2.0 PCR Attestation Audit
audit.tpm_bios.meaning: Interrogates Win32_BIOS and Win32_Tpm to inspect firmware release dates, UEFI Secure Boot enforcement, and TPM 2.0 PCR 0 hardware measurements.

audit.user_accounts.label: User Accounts & Local Admins Audit
audit.user_accounts.meaning: Extracts local user accounts, lockout policies, and members of the built-in Administrators group via Win32_GroupUser to detect unauthorized privilege escalation.

status.compliant.label: Compliant Status
status.compliant.meaning: Assigned when all evaluated CIS Benchmark controls, Microsoft Defender real-time protection, BitLocker volume encryption, and TPM 2.0 attestation pass with zero high-severity policy failures.

status.partial.label: Partial Status
status.partial.meaning: Assigned when non-critical configuration drift is detected — such as an unencrypted secondary data drive, missing non-critical security hotfix, or modified UAC prompt level — while the host remains reachable and authenticated.

status.collection_failed.label: Collection Failed Status
status.collection_failed.meaning: Triggered when the agentless scanner cannot gather host telemetry due to a WinRM connection timeout (port 5986), Kerberos/NTLM authentication rejection (HTTP 401), firewall drop, or invalid RPC credentials.
status.collection_failed.example: Collection Failed (WinRM HTTPS Handshake Timeout on Port 5986)

status.bios_verification.label: BIOS Verification Status
status.bios_verification.meaning: Triggered when hardware root-of-trust checks fail — specifically when UEFI Secure Boot is turned off in firmware, TPM 2.0 chip is disabled or absent, or PCR 0 platform measurement does not match the known golden baseline.
status.bios_verification.example: BIOS Verification (Secure Boot Disabled in UEFI)

health.excellent.label: Excellent Health Band (90.0% – 100.0%)
health.excellent.meaning: Endpoints meet full CIS Level 1 benchmarks with active Defender antivirus definitions updated within 24 hours, BitLocker XTS-AES encryption enforced, and zero known unpatched vulnerabilities.

health.good.label: Good Health Band (75.0% – 89.9%)
health.good.meaning: Endpoints have minor non-critical configuration drift, pending system reboots, or secondary drive exemptions, but have zero CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEVs).

health.fair.label: Fair Health Band (50.0% – 74.9%)
health.fair.meaning: Endpoints exhibit significant security posture lapses, such as missing monthly cumulative updates older than 30 days, disabled UAC prompt enforcement, or missing antivirus signature updates.

health.critical.label: Critical Health Band (< 50.0%)
health.critical.meaning: Endpoints have active CISA KEV remote-code-execution vulnerabilities, disabled Microsoft Defender real-time protection, unencrypted OS boot volumes, or persistent authentication failures.

admin.auto_remediation.label: Automatic Remediation Engine
admin.auto_remediation.meaning: When ON, the system automatically executes signed PowerShell remediation scripts over WinRM to fix drifted settings (e.g. re-enabling Defender or restarting Spooler); risk: automated changes can restart services during peak hours or trigger conflicting Active Directory GPO flapping.
admin.auto_remediation.example: Disabled (Recommended for production until script testing is signed off)

admin.mandatory_bitlocker.label: Mandatory BitLocker Policy
admin.mandatory_bitlocker.meaning: When ON, any endpoint with unencrypted volumes or missing TPM protectors is hard-failed to 0% compliance regardless of other CIS benchmarks; risk: legacy hypervisor virtual machines lacking virtual TPM (vTPM) will immediately breach SLA.
admin.mandatory_bitlocker.example: Enabled (Enforces XTS-AES 256 disk encryption across all laptops)

admin.powershell_introspection.label: Live PowerShell Introspection
admin.powershell_introspection.meaning: When ON, allows execution of dynamic, ad-hoc CIM PowerShell script blocks during scan sweeps for deep registry and event-log analysis; risk: consumes additional CPU cycles on target endpoints and may generate false-positive alerts in third-party EDR/SIEM tools if not allowlisted.
admin.powershell_introspection.example: Enabled (Allows deep forensic and scheduled task indexing)

admin.rollout_tier_pilot.label: Pilot Ring (Canary Tier 5-10%)
admin.rollout_tier_pilot.meaning: When ON, scheduled scan sweeps target canary test machines and lab endpoints first to validate credentials and network latency before broader rollout.

admin.rollout_tier_staged.label: Staged Ring (Departmental Tier 25-50%)
admin.rollout_tier_staged.meaning: When ON, scheduled scan sweeps expand to departmental subnets and non-critical workstations after successful pilot validation.

admin.rollout_tier_full.label: Full Fleet Ring (100% Production)
admin.rollout_tier_full.meaning: When ON, scheduled automated sweeps target all ~400 production servers and endpoints across the enterprise.

admin.retention_strategy.label: Snapshot Retention Strategy
admin.retention_strategy.meaning: Determines whether raw JSONB host introspection payloads older than the retention window are exported to compressed gzip cold storage or pruned down to one golden checkpoint per week.
admin.retention_strategy.format: archive (Compressed GZIP on disk) | downsample (Keep 1 weekly)

admin.retention_window.label: Full-Resolution Retention Window
admin.retention_window.meaning: The number of days full-resolution daily telemetry snapshots are kept in the active PostgreSQL database before being processed by the retention engine.

admin.test_alert_url.label: Target Webhook Endpoint URL
admin.test_alert_url.meaning: The destination HTTPS URL (Slack incoming webhook, Microsoft Teams connector, PagerDuty, or SIEM) that receives synthetic alert notifications to prove alerting reaches human on-call engineers.

admin.bulk_tier_target.label: Target Rollout Tier
admin.bulk_tier_target.meaning: The operational ring (pilot, staged, or full) to which the matched subnets or Active Directory Organizational Units will be reassigned.

admin.bulk_tier_justification.label: Operator Justification Note
admin.bulk_tier_justification.meaning: Mandatory rationale string recorded permanently into the immutable OWASP ASVS audit log for governance and change control tracing.
admin.bulk_tier_justification.example: Subnet 198.51.100.0/24 promoted to Staged after 48h error-free pilot validation

rbac.admin.label: Admin Role Permission Boundary
rbac.admin.meaning: Grants full tenant management, user provisioning, credential rotation via step-up authentication, alert webhook configuration, and retention policy execution.
rbac.admin.example: Full Read/Write/Configure across all modules and credentials

rbac.operator.label: Operator Role Permission Boundary
rbac.operator.meaning: Permits triggering and cancelling agentless scan jobs, acknowledging drift events, and viewing endpoint telemetry, but forbids user administration, credential viewing, or system reconfiguration.
rbac.operator.example: Can launch scans and promote tiers; 403 on user creation and vault secret edits

rbac.auditor.label: Auditor Role Permission Boundary
rbac.auditor.meaning: Provides strictly read-only access to compliance dashboards, vulnerability reports, CIS benchmark evaluations, and immutable security audit logs with zero scan-triggering or modifying privileges.
rbac.auditor.example: Read-only view across reports, audit logs, and compliance grids

rbac.viewer.label: Viewer Role Permission Boundary
rbac.viewer.meaning: Restricted read-only access to high-level fleet overview metrics and endpoint inventory lists, blocked from launching scans, viewing raw audit logs, or generating compliance reports.
rbac.viewer.example: Read-only view of /endpoints and / dashboard only

rbac.superadmin.label: SuperAdmin / Break-Glass Boundary
rbac.superadmin.meaning: Emergency break-glass recovery account with system-wide bypass capabilities, protected by mandatory TOTP multi-factor authentication and writing high-severity audit entries on every action.
rbac.superadmin.example: Direct recovery access during active directory federation outages

endpoint.rollout_tier.label: Rollout Tier
endpoint.rollout_tier.meaning: The assigned operational deployment ring that governs whether this host is included during automated daily scheduled scan sweeps.

endpoint.compliance_score.label: CIS Compliance Score
endpoint.compliance_score.meaning: The percentage of evaluated CIS Windows Benchmark Level 1 recommendations and NIST SP 800-53 security controls passed by this endpoint.

endpoint.bitlocker.label: BitLocker Protection State
endpoint.bitlocker.meaning: Volume encryption status and cryptographic algorithm reported by the Win32_EncryptableVolume CIM provider for the operating system volume.

endpoint.defender.label: Microsoft Defender Antivirus Engine
endpoint.defender.meaning: Real-time file protection state, cloud-delivered malware protection, and definition signature freshness reported by MSFT_MpComputerStatus.

endpoint.tpm.label: TPM 2.0 Security Processor
endpoint.tpm.meaning: Cryptographic hardware security module state, specification version, and PCR 0 platform measurement integrity reported by Win32_Tpm.

report.ttl_hours.label: Shareable Link Expiration Window
report.ttl_hours.meaning: The time duration before the cryptographic HMAC token in the public report link expires and access is automatically revoked.

report.type.label: Audit Report Type
report.type.meaning: Defines the regulatory and structural focus of the generated report: high-level fleet posture, CIS Benchmark compliance breakdown, or CISA KEV vulnerability ledger.
report.type.example: COMPLIANCE_AUDIT (CIS Microsoft Windows Desktop & Server Benchmark)

gateway.fingerprint.label: mTLS Certificate Fingerprint
gateway.fingerprint.meaning: The cryptographic SHA-256 hash of the collector gateway's TLS client certificate, used by the API control plane to verify mutual authentication.
